transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Saturday, October 10. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. 'You cannot put a number': Captain Iyer blames heavy dew after India's defeat. India captain Shreyas Iyer blamed heavy dew and the batting-friendly pitch for his team's six-wicket defeat against West Indies despite scoring 249. He praised Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford for their match-winning partnership. Hope, who scored an unbeaten 102, said partnerships and calculated risks were crucial to completing the challenging chase after West Indies lost two early wickets. Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida as Category 2 storm. Hurricane Isaias has made its presence felt near Destin, Florida, registering maximum sustained winds of 105 mph. Residents in coastal areas across Florida's Panhandle and Alabama are on high alert. In response, officials issued hurricane warnings, with some counties mandating evacuations. To bolster emergency measures, Florida's National Guard mobilized 5,000 personnel, assisting in rescue operations. Idaho family sues after irrigation shutoff ruins crops on 1,000-acre farm. An Idaho family, whose farm thrives along the Snake River, has initiated legal action against the state regarding an emergency order that ceased their irrigation due to dwindling water levels. This abrupt halt has jeopardized their crops and could threaten their agricultural enterprise. They assert that their property rights were infringed upon without due process or fair compensation, highlighting a larger issue surrounding water rights management in the region. Before CJP protest, Delhi bandh: Mobile net, metro, roads blocked in heart of city. Checks at Delhi's borders and barricaded roads inside, mobile internet snapped and metro stations shut , Delhi Police has put in place stringent measures to stop protesters from gathering at Jantar Mantar on Saturday morning. 'Gambhir is chopping and changing': Ex-Australia player calls India 'unsettled'. Former Australian all-rounder Shane Watson criticised Gautam Gambhir for frequently changing India's playing XI and batting order, saying it affects team consistency. However, he praised Gambhir for backing players like Sanju Samson. Meanwhile, West Indies defeated India by six wickets after chasing 250, with Shai Hope scoring an unbeaten 102 to level the five-match T20I series at 1-1. Congress stays away, Left and AAP to join CJP stir against CEC. Cockroach Janta Party's invitation to all opposition parties to join its Oct 10 demonstration against EC's functioning under CEC Gyanesh Kumar saw only the Left, Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool and AAP openly backing its agitation. 1937 Florida ranch now 50,000 acres, among largest US cow-calf ops in 5th gen. Founded in 1937, Adams Ranch in Fort Pierce, Florida, has grown from a small cattle operation into a roughly 50,000-acre ranch spanning several counties. Four generations of the Adams family have worked the land, with a fifth now growing up there. As development expands across Florida, the family remains committed to preserving ranching traditions and supporting local food production. Vance's 'indentured servants' remark deeply offensive: Government. Following a long period of strained India-US ties, the gloves came off finally as India hit out at US Vice President JD Vance for labelling H-1B visa holders and foreign tech professionals as foreign indentured servants, a characterisation New Delhi slammed as deeply offensive and unwarranted. 17-yr-old Indian-American's AI method 68x more efficient, wins $25K scholarship. Pavan Subramani, a 17-year-old Indian-American student from West Virginia, has received a $25,000 Davidson Fellows scholarship for developing an AI-based method to accelerate molecular simulations. His research improved sampling efficiency 68-fold in a specific test and helped simulations reach equilibrium ligand-binding populations more than four times faster, potentially supporting future computational drug discovery research. Jeff Bezos invests $100 million to turn vacant land into parks in eight US cities. Jeff Bezos is putting $100 million into neglected urban land across eight American cities, funding plans to turn vacant plots, former industrial sites and unused spaces into public parks and wildlife habitats. How Jensen Huang's $30M to Stanford University helped open engineering centre. In 2010, Jensen Huang and Lori contributed to establish the Jen-Hsun Huang Engineering Center at Stanford University. The center was designed for collaboration among engineering, science, and medicine students and researchers. It features laboratories, workshops, and a library to support academic pursuits and innovation. Stanford's administration emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary work in modern engineering education.
